question: For observed Palmer penguin records in 2009 with measured flipper length and body mass, does pooled linear regression fitted on 2007–08 give lower mean absolute body-mass error than always predicting the training mean?
unit: One observation (one CSV data row); identify it by its 1-based row number after the header of the pinned file, not by a tracking ID.
split: Assign years 2007 and 2008 to training, 2009 to test. Reject unexpected or absent years. Within each partition omit rows with missing (NA or empty) flipper_length_mm or body_mass_g; retain rows missing unrelated fields. Report totals, retained and excluded for both partitions; no imputation or other exclusions.
arms: On the very same training records, fit (i) an intercept-only predictor equal to the arithmetic mean mass, and (ii) ordinary least squares with intercept predicting mass in grams from flipper length in mm across species. The mean is the intercept-only least-squares baseline, not the constant that minimizes absolute error. No hyperparameter selection, year, species, island, sex, bill, or test observation in the fit.
evaluation: Predict each eligible 2009 row once using its measured flipper length for the linear arm; use measured mass only for eligibility and scoring. Mean absolute error (MAE, g) is the unweighted mean of |prediction - observed mass| on exactly the same test IDs in both arms. Compute baseline MAE minus linear MAE in grams from unrounded values. Strictly positive favors the linear model; zero or negative does not. Report either result.
reproduction: Save one paired row per held-out record with its ID, measurements and both predictions. Report predictions, MAEs and MAE difference to nine decimal places in CSV and error magnitudes to three decimal places in prose (display tolerance 0.0005 g). Require zero difference for reruns at stored precision after ID alignment. Independent floating-point recomputation may differ by up to 0.00000001 g from stored values. Counts must match exactly.
uncertainty_and_scope: This is a descriptive, deterministic comparison for the observed eligible test set. No random seed, confidence interval, hypothesis test or population accuracy claim. Discuss measurement availability, complete-case selection, pooled species and one region/time holdout; do not infer a causal or within-species effect.
data_already_inspected: Before the freeze: public dataset schema, release/rights, byte checksum, and published contextual summaries (including Horst et al.'s pooled trend and species-specific plot). No split-specific fits, test predictions, MAEs or improvement were inspected or computed. This is a teaching demonstration on familiar data, not a blind discovery or externally timestamped preregistration.
budget: Use the one vendored release CSV and Python standard library on one CPU. One deterministic formal comparison; subsequent runs only for reproduction or independent verification. No additional splits, features or model search in response to the score.

criteria.description: Identify the observed data and situate this comparison relative to the published flipper-length/body-mass illustration.
Report the available, complete and excluded records on each side of the year split.
Report both MAEs in grams and their signed difference, and state which method, if either, does better for these records.
